title: Transboundary haze — Singapore · Indonesia (2026)
description: Since August 2026, fires in Indonesia, mostly in Kalimantan and Sumatra, have sent haze across Singapore and Malaysia in what reporting calls the worst fire season in a decade. In October Singapore's environment agency issued preventive measures notices to ten Indonesia-based companies under its 2014 haze act, though no company has ever been prosecuted under it. Indonesia says it has deployed more than 60,000 personnel and dozens of aircraft, its president has pledged to expose foreign companies he says are also responsible, and Jakarta has given mixed signals on accepting outside help. The two governments must settle who holds companies accountable, whether foreign firefighting help is accepted and under whose command, what fire and concession data Indonesia shares with Singapore, and who pays for peatland restoration. The crisis is ongoing: there is no known outcome. Positions are reconstructed from public reporting and are not official.

sources.title: Southeast Asia's toxic haze spurs calls for legal action against polluters
facts: Fires in Indonesia are estimated to have burned more than 2 million hectares this season (Al Jazeera estimate).
Singapore's National Environment Agency has issued notices to 10 Indonesia-based firms this season; no company has ever been prosecuted under Singapore's 2014 haze act.
The ASEAN haze agreement's coordinating office in Jakarta only opened in April 2026, and the treaty has no judicial enforcement body.
President Prabowo Subianto pledged to expose foreign companies he said were also responsible, said people found starting fires had been arrested, and said the government would step up its response.
Malaysia and Singapore have refrained from criticising Indonesia and have offered help fighting the fires; Jakarta has given mixed signals on accepting outside help.

sources.title: Singapore expands crackdown on Indonesian companies linked to haze
facts: Singapore issued preventive measures notices to seven companies linked to fires in Sumatra (16 October) and three more with concessions in Kalimantan (19 October).
The notices require the companies to send firefighters to their land, stop burning and submit plans to prevent recurrence; they are not a finding of legal responsibility.
Singapore's environment minister said the haze could persist and reach hazardous levels, with improvement expected in three to four weeks as the inter-monsoon season arrives.

sources.title: Indonesia, Malaysia maintain talks as transboundary haze persists
facts: Malaysia's Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim contacted President Prabowo about the haze and said Malaysia was ready to help.
Anwar asked for a meeting of ASEAN environment ministers to coordinate the response.
Indonesia's foreign minister said more than 60,000 personnel had been deployed, with 61 aircraft on standby (44 for water-bombing, 17 for patrols and weather modification).
Indonesia's forestry ministry reported 793 hotspots nationwide, up from 437 the previous day; Central Kalimantan had the most, 288.

sources.title: DOE: Transboundary haze thickens, 1,211 hotspots detected in southern Asean, mostly in Kalimantan
facts: 1,211 hotspots were detected in the southern ASEAN region: 1,180 in Kalimantan, 18 in Sumatra and 13 in Malaysia.

sources.title: ASEAN Agreement on Transboundary Haze Pollution (2002), full text
facts: Article 3(1): parties keep the sovereign right to exploit their own resources, with a duty not to cause environmental damage to other states.
Article 8(1): each party's monitoring centre must send fire and haze data to the ASEAN Co-ordinating Centre at agreed intervals.
Article 27: disputes are settled amicably by consultation or negotiation; there is no court or tribunal.

sources.title: Transboundary Haze Pollution Act 2014 (No. 24 of 2014)
facts: Section 4: the Act extends to conduct outside Singapore.
Section 5(2)(a): a fine of up to S$100,000 for every day of haze pollution in Singapore; section 5(5): the aggregate fine is capped at S$2 million.
Section 8: an entity owning or occupying land where a fire burns is presumed to have caused the haze, and ownership can be proved from maps supplied by a foreign government.

sources.title: Haze press conference: opening remarks by Ms Grace Fu
sources.publisher: Ministry of Sustainability and the Environment, Singapore, 16 October 2026
facts: Singapore offered Indonesia civilian firefighting assistance and cloud-seeding support; the minister had not yet heard back.
The Chief Executive Officer of Singapore's National Environment Agency (NEA) wrote to and called her Indonesian counterparts to offer support.
NEA will issue preventive measures notices to seven companies, will issue notices to more, and will consider further action under the haze act where the evidence warrants.
Singapore began distributing haze masks to vulnerable Singaporeans on 14 October; about 10% of those eligible had collected them.
Groups named as more vulnerable to haze: seniors, pregnant women, young children, and people with chronic heart or lung conditions.
The minister said the haze episode may last a few more weeks, improving with the inter-monsoon period in about three to four weeks.

sources.title: Indonesia's haze response draws ire at home and abroad
sources.publisher: The Jakarta Post, via Asia News Network, 19 October 2026
facts: Indonesia's foreign minister said President Prabowo had approved accepting foreign assistance, with offers being discussed at the technical level at BNPB, Indonesia's disaster management agency.
A Malaysian politician called for ASEAN financial pressure on the companies behind the fires; Malaysia's foreign minister called a formal protest a last resort.
